# Awtsmoos Studio Unification — Mission and Evidence

> From one hidden source the many frames arise; the Awtsmoos renews every pixel before our eyes.  
> At Awtsmoos.com the vessels may differ in face, while one truthful contract gives every studio its place.

## Mission

Build a shared movie-making foundation for Geelooy that lets AI author real timed 2D, 3D, and hybrid productions: characters, shapes, paths, text, particles, tutorials, infographics, camera language, transitions, audio/captions, procedural assets, and export. Preserve distinct product personalities while sharing one canonical movie contract and reusable engines. Create a mobile-first `awtsmoos-studio` that combines the shared capabilities and prove the system with a real 180-second movie.

## Direct Repository Evidence

- `apps/animator` already contains AI command routing, character performance, camera planning, studio film UI, procedural generators, render pipelines, and movie-export machinery.
- `apps/nesher-studio` contains mature NLE concepts, effects/particles, audio, WebCodecs/WebM/MP4-oriented export code, timeline/project models, and scene-graph tooling.
- `apps/slides` contains declarative element composition, procedural authoring, mobile-oriented UI, and compact render abstractions valuable for text/shape/tutorial scenes.
- `apps/mitzvah-studio` contains a focused document/object/canvas/editor model suitable as a 2D adapter personality.
- `apps/video-editor` contains another timeline/editor personality that should converge on the same movie contract rather than duplicate it.
- `libs/awtsmoos-procedural-core` already contains animation, 3D text, human scene objects, creature systems, physics, liquids, particles, particle presets, procedural objects, scene timeline handlers, and Three.js adapters.
- As observed before implementation, no `apps/awtsmoos-studio`, no `libs/awtsmoos-ui`, and no `libs/awtsmoos-procedural-core/src/core/movie` namespace existed.
- The working tree is already heavily dirty, especially Animator, Mitzvah Studio, and portions of procedural core. Concurrent agents are active. Existing dirty files must not be casually rewritten.

## Hard Safety and Quality Constraints

1. Prefer new modules and adapters over collision-prone rewrites.
2. Re-read any existing file immediately before a full-file rewrite.
3. Never partially patch an existing file.
4. Keep executable source files at or below 120 lines where practical; split responsibilities aggressively.
5. Use tabs for code indentation, descriptive names, readable line breaks, and JSDoc.
6. Keep browser/mobile behavior first-class, not an afterthought.
7. Build code first, then tests and runtime verification.
8. Verification must include syntax/import checks, contract tests, 180-second feature coverage, app/browser smoke, responsive checks, and export/probe evidence when available.

## Work Graph Roots

- Shared movie contract and compiler in procedural core.
- Shared procedural movie asset catalog that exposes existing 2D/3D generation through one AI-facing vocabulary.
- Shared Awtsmoos UI JSON-to-DOM system with accessible mobile studio recipes.
- New Awtsmoos Studio application consuming both libraries.
- Adapters/profiles for Animator, Nesher Studio, Mitzvah Studio, Video Editor, and Slides.
- A 180-second production fixture with multiple scenes, cameras, characters, particles, text, shapes, infographic/tutorial beats, 2D/3D layers, and transitions.
- Tests, browser verification, export verification, read-back, delta review, and handoff.

## Evidence Standard

No claim is complete because a file exists. Completion requires observed behavior. Every success creates shadow work: tests, read-back, integration review, mobile review, export review, and documentation. Remaining work stays open until those proofs exist.
